Recommend a verification method for each obligation, from the catalog.

USAGE
  $ quoin advise [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--module <value>] [--mismatch-only] [--inconclusive-only]
    [--json]

FLAGS
  --inconclusive-only  Only obligations no rule matched. Combines with
                       --mismatch-only as a union.
  --json               Emit the advice as JSON.
  --mismatch-only      Only genuine disagreements: the authored method is a
                       declared method or class and is not among the
                       recommendations. Uncatalogued values are not mismatches.
                       Combines with --inconclusive-only as a union.
  --module=<value>     Module directory supplying the traceability model.
  --repo=<value>       [default: .] Repository root.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Recommend a verification method for each obligation, from the catalog.

  The deterministic half of the test-plan advisor (FR-031). Rules match or they
  do
  not; where they are inconclusive it says so and stops, rather than guessing.

  Before this, the method table was skill-local prose and `Verification` columns
  defaulted to Test by habit — nothing ever advised DAST for an attack surface,
  monitors for a temporal property, or fault injection for a reliability NFR.

  Obligations come from quire (coverage --json), and each criterion's FR-052
  property shape from quire (properties --json), so the advice is over what the
  spec actually states rather than over a document somebody pasted in.

  Read the output as a recommendation, never a verdict. An LLM may judge the
  residue afterwards — labelled as judgement (the FR-042 / ADR-0010 discipline).

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin advise

  $ quoin advise --mismatch-only

  $ quoin advise --json

Render the assurance case: claim → argument → evidence, from the store.

USAGE
  $ quoin assurance [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--module <value>] [--claim-type <value>...]
    [--independence-policy <value>] [--argument <value>] [--decisions <value>]
    [--discharge <value>] [--as-of <value>] [--json]

FLAGS
  --argument=<value>
      Render the authored AssuranceArgument with this frontmatter id. Requires
      --decisions and --as-of; cannot be combined with --claim-type.

  --as-of=<value>
      Explicit ISO-8601 instant for authored argument evaluation.

  --claim-type=<value>...
      Artifact type that is a top-level claim. Repeatable; matched
      case-insensitively. REPLACES the StR default rather than adding to it — pass
      --claim-type StR as well if StRs should stay claims. A safety or security
      bundle argues from a declared hazard or threat.

  --decisions=<value>
      JSON array of explicit sufficiency decisions.

  --discharge=<value>
      Optional clause-discharge-v1 report JSON path.

  --independence-policy=<value>
      Normalized JSON projection of exact obligation/dimension requirements
      selected by an AssuranceProfile.

  --json
      Emit the case as JSON.

  --module=<value>
      Module directory supplying the traceability model.

  --repo=<value>
      [default: .] Repository root.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Render the assurance case: claim → argument → evidence, from the store.

  A pile of green evidence is not an argument (FR-040). This view makes the
  reasoning reviewable: this claim holds BECAUSE these sub-claims hold, EACH
  verified by a stated method, WITH evidence that is fresh.

  Strictly a view. It runs nothing, collects nothing and writes nothing to the
  store — where the case cannot be built, the missing data is a finding against
  the spec, not something this fabricates.

  Gaps render as OPEN nodes (◇), not as omissions. An undischarged obligation, a
  suspect binding or a claim nothing traces to stays in the tree, because a case
  that quietly narrows to what it can prove reads exactly like a complete one.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin assurance

  $ quoin assurance --claim-type StR --claim-type hazard

  $ quoin assurance > docs/assurance.md

Form, retain, and verify change-assurance evidence from explicit inputs.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Form, retain, and verify change-assurance evidence from explicit inputs.

  Producer-facing surface over the FR-063 record, FR-064 proof attestation,
  retained-output intake, and FR-065 verification receipt contracts (FR-068).

  These commands transcribe and verify what a producer supplies. None of them
  runs the command an attestation describes, invokes Git, or performs a network
  request. The only process any of them starts is the quoin-core engine that
  decides the FR-063..FR-065 contracts (FR-096). Digests establish content
  integrity and recorded
  actor labels are attribution only; nothing here establishes authorization or
  non-repudiation, and no output is a certification.

  Subcommands:
  quoin change-assurance seal-record
  quoin change-assurance seal-attestation
  quoin change-assurance intake
  quoin change-assurance receipt
  quoin change-assurance verify-receipt
  quoin change-assurance schema
  quoin change-assurance recover

  Exit status: 0 for a valid receipt, 1 for an invalid or incomplete one, and 2
  for a usage, parse, or integrity error.

COMMANDS
  change-assurance intake            Retain an exact sealed attestation and its
                                     exact output bytes.
  change-assurance receipt           Verify a candidate from retained inputs and
                                     emit its receipt.
  change-assurance recover           Remove staging directories left by an
                                     interrupted intake.
  change-assurance schema            Emit a packaged change-assurance JSON
                                     Schema asset.
  change-assurance seal-attestation  Seal a proof attestation over an existing
                                     retained result file.
  change-assurance seal-record       Seal an explicit change-assurance record
                                     and retain it.
  change-assurance verify-receipt    Re-verify a sealed verification receipt.

Retain an exact sealed attestation and its exact output bytes.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance intake --attestation <value> --output <value>
    [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config] [--repo <value>] [--json]

FLAGS
  --attestation=<value>  (required) Exact sealed attestation JSON. `-` reads
                         stdin.
  --json                 Emit canonical JSON.
  --output=<value>       (required) Exact retained result file the attestation
                         names. Its bytes are retained and re-hashed; it is
                         never executed.
  --repo=<value>         [default: .] Repository root for retained Quoin state.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Retain an exact sealed attestation and its exact output bytes.

  Verifies ONE sealed attestation against the bytes it claims and retains the
  pair atomically: either both the attestation JSON and the output file become
  visible together, or neither does.

  The retained attestation is the canonical form of what was supplied and the
  retained output is byte-for-byte the file named by --output. A recorded digest
  or size that contradicts those bytes is refused and nothing is retained.

  Re-running with byte-identical inputs succeeds and retains nothing new. The
  same digest with different bytes is a collision and is refused.

  An interrupted intake leaves an invisible staging directory that is never read
  as an attestation; `quoin change-assurance recover` removes it.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance intake --attestation attestation.json --output junit.xml --json

Verify a candidate from retained inputs and emit its receipt.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance receipt --record <value> --candidate-revision <value>
    --decisions <value> [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config] [--parent
    <value>...] [--select <value>...] [--audits <value>] [--repo <value>]
    [--json]

FLAGS
  --audits=<value>              Retained FR-032 audit reports as a JSON array.
                                Absent means no audit was retained, which stays
                                distinct from an audit with no findings.
  --candidate-revision=<value>  (required) Candidate revision the selected
                                attestations must be bound to.
  --decisions=<value>           (required) Retained ix-flow decision history
                                JSON (`run_id` plus its exact event chain). `-`
                                reads stdin.
  --json                        Emit canonical JSON.
  --parent=<value>...           [default: ] Digest of a stored parent record,
                                repeated for each earlier revision. Named rather
                                than walked, so a missing ancestor is a stated
                                gap instead of a silently shortened chain.
  --record=<value>              (required) Digest of the stored change-assurance
                                record to verify.
  --repo=<value>                [default: .] Repository root for retained Quoin
                                state.
  --select=<value>...           [default: ] Explicit
                                `<proof-id>=<attestation-digest>` selection,
                                repeated per proof. Only selected attestations
                                are read.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Verify a candidate from retained inputs and emit its receipt.

  Assembles the FR-065 verification input from what the caller names — the
  stored record, its parents, the explicitly selected attestations and their
  retained outputs, the retained ix-flow decision history, and any retained
  FR-032 audit reports — and emits the resulting receipt.

  Nothing is discovered. A stored attestation that is not named by --select has
  no effect on the receipt, so a stray upload cannot discharge a proof.

  No proof, suite, tool, workflow, Git, or network operation runs, and nothing
  is
  written. Missing evidence stays missing: `unavailable`, `not_computed`, and
  absent attestations remain their own outcomes and reasons and are never turned
  into a pass or a failure.

  Exit status is 0 for a `valid` receipt and 1 for an `invalid` or
  `incomplete` one. The receipt is emitted either way; a usage, parse, or
  integrity error exits 2 instead and emits none.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance receipt --record <record-digest> --candidate-revision <sha> --select PROOF-1=<attestation-digest> --decisions decisions.json --json

Remove staging directories left by an interrupted intake.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance recover [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--json]

FLAGS
  --json          Emit canonical JSON.
  --repo=<value>  [default: .] Repository root for retained Quoin state.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Remove staging directories left by an interrupted intake.

  Intake makes an attestation and its output visible with a single rename. If it
  is interrupted before that rename, the half-written pair stays in a staging
  directory that is never read as an attestation — invisible, but not free.

  This removes exactly those staging directories and reports how many it
  removed.
  Retained records, attestations, and outputs are left untouched, and nothing
  here re-runs, re-hashes, or re-verifies anything.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance recover --repo . --json

Emit a packaged change-assurance JSON Schema asset.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance schema [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--name change-assurance-record-v1.schema.json|proof-attestation-v1.schema.j
    son|verification-receipt-v1.schema.json] [--json]

FLAGS
  --json           Emit canonical JSON.
  --name=<option>  Schema asset to emit.
                   <options: change-assurance-record-v1.schema.json|proof-attest
                   ation-v1.schema.json|verification-receipt-v1.schema.json>

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Emit a packaged change-assurance JSON Schema asset.

  Prints one of the three normative, versioned schema assets shipped with this
  build, byte-for-byte as the engine carries them, so a consumer validates
  against the same file the sealing and verification code was written against
  rather than a copy that has drifted.

  Without --name the three asset names are listed. An unknown name is refused.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance schema

  $ quoin change-assurance schema --name proof-attestation-v1.schema.json

Seal a proof attestation over an existing retained result file.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance seal-attestation --input <value> --output <value> --media-type
    <value> [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config] [--json]

FLAGS
  --input=<value>       (required) Proof-attestation body as JSON, without
                        `digest` and without `retained_output`. `-` reads stdin.
  --json                Emit canonical JSON.
  --media-type=<value>  (required) Declared media type of the retained result
                        file. Stated by the caller rather than sniffed, so a
                        producer's own content type is preserved exactly.
  --output=<value>      (required) Path of the retained result file this
                        attestation describes. Its bytes are hashed and
                        measured; it is never executed.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Seal a proof attestation over an existing retained result file.

  Binds ONE already-produced result file to the reviewed record, candidate
  revision, proof obligation, command, tool, configuration, environment, and
  result the caller states (FR-064), and emits the sealed attestation JSON.

  The ONLY fields derived here are `retained_output.digest` and
  `retained_output.size_bytes`, read from the bytes of --output, plus the
  `media_type` the caller declares. Everything else is the caller's: this
  command does not run the proof command, re-read the tool, inspect the
  repository, or infer a result from the file it hashes. A body supplying
  `retained_output` or `digest` is refused.

  The attestation is emitted, not retained. `quoin change-assurance intake`
  is the retention step, and it re-checks this binding against the same bytes.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance seal-attestation --input attestation.json --output junit.xml --media-type application/xml

Seal an explicit change-assurance record and retain it.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance seal-record --input <value> [--config-root <value>]
    [--no-project-config] [--repo <value>] [--json]

FLAGS
  --input=<value>  (required) Change-assurance record body as JSON, without
                   `digest`. `-` reads stdin.
  --json           Emit canonical JSON.
  --repo=<value>   [default: .] Repository root for retained Quoin state.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Seal an explicit change-assurance record and retain it.

  Seals ONE reviewed change definition the caller supplies in full (FR-063) and
  retains it under its own digest.

  The body is the record without its `digest`: the digest is computed from the
  canonical bytes of everything else, so supplying one is refused rather than
  overwritten. Nothing in the body is inferred, defaulted, or discovered — a
  field the caller did not state is a validation failure, not a blank.

  This command runs no producer and reads no repository state beyond the store
  it writes into.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance seal-record --input record.json --json

  cat record.json | quoin change-assurance seal-record --input -

Re-verify a sealed verification receipt.

USAGE
  $ quoin change-assurance verify-receipt --input <value> [--config-root <value>]
    [--no-project-config] [--json]

FLAGS
  --input=<value>  (required) Sealed verification receipt JSON. `-` reads stdin.
  --json           Emit canonical JSON.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Re-verify a sealed verification receipt.

  Checks that a receipt still has the shape FR-065 declares and still hashes to
  its own digest, so an edited outcome, reason, proof row, or check is refused
  rather than read back as fact.

  This re-verifies the receipt document. It does not re-run verification: the
  underlying record, attestations, and decisions are not consulted, and no proof
  command is executed.

  Exit status is 0 when the verified receipt is `valid`, 1 when it is
  `invalid` or `incomplete`, and 2 when the document itself is refused.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin change-assurance verify-receipt --input receipt.json --json

Report which declared vocabulary values no requirement owns, and judge the excuses.

USAGE
  $ quoin completeness [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--bundle <value>] [--module <value>] [--strict] [--json]

FLAGS
  --bundle=<value>  Bundle root to read. Defaults to <repo>/spec, the directory
                    quire treats as the bundle.
  --json            Emit the report as JSON.
  --module=<value>  Module directory supplying the vocabulary declarations.
  --repo=<value>    [default: .] Repository root.
  --strict          Exit non-zero when any value is unowned, not only on a high
                    finding.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Report which declared vocabulary values no requirement owns, and judge the
  excuses.

  The verdict half of declared-vocabulary coverage (FR-037). quire-rs FR-059
  computes which declared values no document claims — a deterministic fact about
  the spec. This decides what a gap is worth, and whether an exclusion was
  earned.

  The first vocabulary is ISO 25010: a bundle can be 100% AC-covered and still
  have no requirement anywhere for reliability, security or maintainability. The
  characteristic list is module data (12 values, not the 9 the ticket assumed),
  so
  nothing here is hardcoded — it is read from the same declaration the engine
  reads.

  A value may be excused. "This is a CLI that controls no physical process, so
  it
  has no safety characteristic" is an answer, and a check that cannot accept one
  forces either a permanent false finding or a requirement fabricated to silence
  it. But the engine accepts a bare list: adding one frontmatter line took this
  repository from 7 findings to 5 with no reason written anywhere. So an
  exclusion
  must carry a written reason, in the same document, in a table row naming the
  value.

  Severities are deliberately asymmetric. An unowned characteristic is medium —
  an admitted gap a reader can see. An unjustified exclusion is high: an
  assertion
  of completeness with nothing behind it, which also removes the finding that
  would have prompted the work.

  Advisory by default. --strict makes an admitted gap fail too; it does not
  invent
  one.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin completeness

  $ quoin completeness --strict

  $ quoin completeness --json

  $ quoin completeness --repo ../other-repo

  inspections.md   authored inspection acts    (validated corpus document)

Re-affirm a binding after the statement it was made against changed.

USAGE
  $ quoin evidence affirm --obligation <value> --who <value> [--config-root
    <value>] [--no-project-config] [--note <value>] [--commit <value>] [--repo
    <value>] [--module <value>] [--json]

FLAGS
  --commit=<value>      Commit of the affirmation. Defaults to HEAD.
  --json                Emit the outcome as JSON.
  --module=<value>      Module directory supplying the traceability model.
  --note=<value>        Why the evidence still holds.
  --obligation=<value>  (required) Obligation id whose binding is being
                        re-affirmed.
  --repo=<value>        [default: .] Repository root.
  --who=<value>         (required) Who is affirming. Recorded verbatim.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Re-affirm a binding after the statement it was made against changed.

  A reworded acceptance criterion changes its content hash, which makes every
  binding on it SUSPECT until somebody says the evidence still discharges the
  new
  wording. This is that act.

  Auto-bind, explicit affirmation: first discharge binds without asking, because
  requiring a signature on something the evidence already proves puts a gate in
  front of the common case and teaches people to click through it.
  Re-affirmation
  is the judgement call, so it stays explicit — and it is recorded with who, at
  which commit, and optionally why.

  Re-running the test does NOT clear suspicion. If it did, the suspect state
  would
  clear itself on the next CI run and the detector would never fire.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin evidence affirm --obligation FR-001-AC-1 --who @reviewer

  $ quoin evidence affirm --obligation NFR-006-M-2 --who @reviewer --note 'threshold widened deliberately'

Audit the evidence store: suspect links, staleness, vacuity.

USAGE
  $ quoin evidence audit [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--module <value>...] [--ratchet] [--strict] [--json]
    [--multiplicity-requires <value>...] [--mutation-floor <value>...]
    [--independence-policy <value>]

FLAGS
  --independence-policy=<value>       Normalized JSON projection of exact
                                      obligation/dimension requirements selected
                                      by an AssuranceProfile. Unset means no
                                      independence policy.
  --json                              Emit the report as JSON.
  --module=<value>...                 Module directory supplying the
                                      traceability model. Repeatable; roots are
                                      used in the order given and replace
                                      ambient discovery entirely rather than
                                      adding to it.
  --multiplicity-requires=<value>...  Criticality values demanding two
                                      independent suites. Repeatable. Unset by
                                      default: no obligation source in the
                                      ecosystem declares a criticality column,
                                      so a built-in default could never fire.
  --mutation-floor=<value>...         Minimum mutation score per criticality, as
                                      <criticality>=<0..1>. Repeatable. Unset by
                                      default, for the same reason as
                                      --multiplicity-requires: a built-in floor
                                      is a rule nobody chose.
  --ratchet                           Report only violations absent from the
                                      baseline.
  --repo=<value>                      [default: .] Repository root.
  --strict                            Exit 1 when any reported finding remains.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Audit the evidence store: suspect links, staleness, vacuity.

  Reads the store and reports. RUNS NOTHING (ADR-0011 invariant 1) — the
  consumer's CI refreshes evidence, and an auditor that could re-run a suite
  could
  also make a finding disappear by re-running it.

  Checks:
  suspect-link      the statement changed after the evidence was bound
  stale-evidence    bound to a missing run, or to a run behind HEAD
  vacuous-evidence  every bound symbol was skipped or absent from the run
  undischarged      no evidence is bound at all
  method-conformance   evidence of a kind the declared method does not produce
  unknown-method       the declared method is in no catalog
  insufficient-multiplicity   criticality demands two independent suites
  insufficient-mutation-score criticality demands a mutation score it misses
  unmeasured-mutation-score   a demanded mutation score, with none recorded
  insufficient-independence  profile-selected evidence separation is absent

  --ratchet compares against spec/evidence/baseline.json and fails only on NEW
  violations. A gate that fails on the whole existing backlog gets disabled
  within
  a week. Write that baseline with: quoin evidence baseline

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin evidence audit

  $ quoin evidence audit --ratchet --strict

  $ quoin evidence audit --json

Accept the current findings as the ratchet baseline.

USAGE
  $ quoin evidence baseline [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--module <value>] [--dry-run] [--json]

FLAGS
  --dry-run         Print what would be accepted and write nothing.
  --json            Emit the outcome as JSON.
  --module=<value>  Module directory supplying the traceability model.
  --repo=<value>    [default: .] Repository root.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Accept the current findings as the ratchet baseline.

  Writes spec/evidence/baseline.json: every finding the audit reports right now,
  as <kind>:<obligation>, plus the commit it was accepted at.

  `--ratchet` reads this file and fails only on findings NOT in it. Without it,
  a first run of the gate reports the entire existing backlog and gets switched
  off within a week — so accepting a baseline is the deliberate act that makes
  the ratchet usable, and its diff is the record of what was accepted and by
  whom.

  Re-run this at a release to move the ratchet forward. Never run it to make a
  new failure go away: the diff is reviewed, and a baseline that grows between
  releases is the gate quietly being disabled one entry at a time.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin evidence baseline

  $ quoin evidence baseline --dry-run

Drop run records nothing references.

USAGE
  $ quoin evidence gc [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config]
    [--repo <value>] [--dry-run] [--json]

FLAGS
  --dry-run       List what would be deleted without deleting it.
  --json          Emit the deleted paths as JSON.
  --repo=<value>  [default: .] Repository root.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.

DESCRIPTION
  Drop run records nothing references.

  Retention policy: the latest run per suite, plus anything a binding points at.

  Dir-per-suite is what makes this local — a policy change for one expensive
  suite
  (mutation, DAST, fuzz) touches one directory, and a .gitignore decision can be
  made per suite rather than for the whole store.

  Takes no --module, deliberately, though every sibling command does: --module
  supplies the traceability model to quire, and gc never invokes quire and never
  loads a catalog. It is a repo-scoped store operation — it walks runs/ and
  scans/ under spec/evidence/ and decides from timestamps and bindings alone,
  none of which carry catalog semantics. Should retention ever become
  module-policy-driven, the flag stops being a no-op and gets added then (#171).

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin evidence gc --dry-run

  $ quoin evidence gc

Transcribe one suite run into the evidence store.

USAGE
  $ quoin evidence record --suite <value> --commit <value> --tool <value>
    --results <value> [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config] [--kind
    <value>] [--lineage <value>] [--discharges <value>] [--adapter
    entries|junit|cargo-mutants|sbom|agent-eval|contract-conformance|differentia
    l-report|sarif|audit-script|cargo-audit] [--repo <value>] [--module <value>]
    [--timestamp <value>] [--json]

FLAGS
  --adapter=<option>
      Format reader for --results (entries, junit, cargo-mutants, sbom,
      agent-eval, contract-conformance, differential-report, sarif, audit-script,
      cargo-audit). Defaults to the adapter claiming --tool, else the normalized
      shape. An unknown name is an error rather than a silent fall back, so a typo
      reports itself instead of failing later as a JSON-shape complaint.
      <options: entries|junit|cargo-mutants|sbom|agent-eval|contract-conformance|d
      ifferential-report|sarif|audit-script|cargo-audit>

  --commit=<value>
      (required) Full commit sha the run was performed at.

  --discharges=<value>
      Obligation ids this scan discharges, comma-separated. Finding-shaped only. A
      CLEAN scan is the strongest evidence a scanner produces and carries no
      finding to bind from, so the obligations it was run to check are stated
      rather than inferred. A scan that evaluated no rules binds nothing
      regardless.

  --json
      Emit the outcome as JSON.

  --kind=<value>
      Evidence kind this run produced (Unit, Property, Static, Manual, …) — the
      vocabulary the catalog's `evidence_kind` and the suite registry's `Evidence
      Kind` column use. Method conformance compares kind to kind; without it the
      check stays silent rather than guessing.

  --lineage=<value>
      JSON file naming profile-relevant evidence lineage: actor,
      implementationToolchain, technique, dataSource, and/or reviewPath. These are
      relationship facts, not an independence verdict.

  --module=<value>
      Module directory supplying the traceability model.

  --repo=<value>
      [default: .] Repository root. Defaults to the working directory.

  --results=<value>
      (required) Normalized run entries as JSON. `-` reads stdin.

  --suite=<value>
      (required) Suite id from spec/evidence/suites.md (e.g. SUITE-001).

  --timestamp=<value>
      ISO-8601 run time. Defaults to now.

  --tool=<value>
      (required) Tool and version, as it identifies itself.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Transcribe one suite run into the evidence store.

  Records ONE run of ONE suite at ONE commit, then binds every obligation that
  run discharged, stamping the statement hash as it stands now.

  quoin transcribes; the consumer's CI executes (ADR-0011 invariant 1). This
  command runs no test and judges no result — recording a FAILING run is as
  legitimate as recording a passing one, and more useful, because a suite that
  stopped passing is exactly what a freshness check needs to see.

  --results takes normalized entries:

  {"entries": [{"symbol": "tests::tc001", "outcome": "pass", "traceIds":
  ["FR-001-AC-1"]}]}

  --adapter selects a format reader. Without it the suite's --tool picks one,
  and
  failing that the normalized shape above is assumed. An adapter transcribes; it
  runs nothing and judges nothing.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin evidence record --suite SUITE-001 --commit $(git rev-parse HEAD) --tool 'cargo test 1.94.1' --results run.json

Classify every Markdown artifact's Properties form across corpus roots (FR-074).

USAGE

    [--config-root <value>] [--no-project-config] [--out <value>]

ARGUMENTS

    [--repo <value>] [--strict] [--json]

FLAGS

  Validate repository QA gates and report located defects.

Build an authoring pack for spec files an agent is about to create or edit.

USAGE
  $ quoin write [REPO_DIR] [--config-root <value>]
    [--no-project-config] [--types <value>...] [--org <value>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS
  [REPO_DIR]  Target repository directory.

FLAGS
  --json              Emit the authoring pack as JSON.
  --org=<value>       Authoring organization. Overrides QUOIN_ORG and the repo's
                      origin remote.
  --types=<value>...  Artifact/object type(s), comma-separated or repeated.

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --config-root=<value>  [env: IX_CONFIG_ROOT] Override the user-level config
                         root for this invocation.
  --no-project-config    Disable project-local .ix config layering.

DESCRIPTION
  Build an authoring pack for spec files an agent is about to create or edit.

  Pass the target repository and the artifact/object types involved in the work.
  quoin resolves those types from the active catalog and returns the local
  skeletons, schemas, module roots, and Quire validation command for the repo.

  Notes:
  - Type lookup is case-insensitive; FR and fr are the same type.
  - Types can be artifacts or objects from the default module set or modules.
  - Use the returned skeletons and schemas as the authoring contract.
  - Run the returned Quire command after editing spec files.
  - The org is resolved from --org, else QUOIN_ORG, else the repo's origin
  remote. It is never defaulted: put the reported org in the frontmatter
  "org:" field rather than copying a value from a skeleton.

EXAMPLES
  $ quoin write . --types FR

  $ quoin write . --types FR,domain,entity

  $ quoin write ../my-service --types fr,DOMAIN --json

  $ quoin write . --types Spec --org acme
